description: A garlic-forward Kenyan chicken stew where plenty of crushed garlic is cooked with chicken pieces, onions and tomatoes to create a rich, aromatic sauce.

steps.instruction: Crush the garlic cloves and set aside. Heat oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken pieces on all sides for 6–8 minutes.
Add chopped onions and cook until soft and golden, about 5 minutes. Stir in the crushed garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes break down into a thick sauce.
Return the chicken to the pot, add water, cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce coats the meat.
Adjust salt and serve hot with ugali, rice or chapati.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and sukuma wiki.

description: A warming Kenyan tea brewed with fresh ginger, milk and sugar—served daily in homes and roadside cafes across the country.

steps.instruction: Peel and grate or crush the fresh ginger. Bring water to a boil in a small pot.
Add the ginger and boil for 2 minutes to release its flavour.
Pour in the milk and add sugar. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 4–5 minutes.
Strain into cups and serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with chapati or mandazi for breakfast.

description: A vibrant Kenyan chicken curry where fresh coriander and yogurt form the base of the sauce, giving a bright green, herbaceous dish.

steps.instruction: Blend fresh coriander, yogurt, garlic, ginger and green pepper (if using) into a smooth green paste.
Heat oil and brown the chicken pieces for 6–8 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onions until golden. Return the chicken and stir in the coriander-yogurt paste.
Add salt and simmer on low heat for 15–20 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the sauce thickens. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or chapati.

description: Fluffy rice cooked with turmeric and aromatic vegetables, giving a golden colour and earthy flavour—a simple Kenyan side dish.

steps.instruction: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Heat oil in a pot and sauté chopped onion and carrot (if using) until soft.
Stir in the turmeric and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the rice and stir to coat with the turmeric mixture. Pour in water and add salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 18–20 minutes until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed. Fluff and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with beef stew or grilled chicken.

description: A fragrant Kenyan spiced rice dish cooked with pilau masala, beef and caramelised onions—a festive staple at celebrations and weddings.

steps.instruction: Heat oil in a heavy pot. Add sliced onions and fry on medium heat until deep golden brown, about 12–15 minutes.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger and pilau masala. Stir and fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add beef cubes and brown on all sides. Pour in 2 cups of water, cover and simmer until the beef is tender, about 30 minutes.
Add washed rice and the remaining water. Season with salt, stir once, cover tightly and cook on low heat for 20 minutes until the rice absorbs all the liquid.
Remove from heat and let steam for 5 minutes. Fluff gently and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with kachumbari and a cold drink.

description: Sweet triangular fried dough from the Kenyan coast, perfumed with ground cardamom and enriched with coconut milk.

steps.instruction: Grate the coconut and squeeze to extract about 1 cup of coconut milk.
Mix flour, ground cardamom, sugar and salt in a bowl. Add the coconut milk and egg (if using) and knead into a soft dough.
Cover the dough and let it rest for 20 minutes. Divide into small balls and roll each into a thin circle, then cut into triangles.
Heat oil in a deep pan and fry the triangles in batches for 2–3 minutes per side until golden brown. Drain and serve warm.

serving_suggestion: Serve with Kenyan chai for breakfast.

description: Soft Kenyan chapati infused with ground cinnamon, adding a warm sweetness to the layered flatbread.

steps.instruction: Mix flour, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl. Add water gradually and knead into a soft, smooth dough.
Divide the dough into 6–8 balls. Cover and let rest for 30 minutes.
Roll each ball into a thin circle. Brush with oil, fold into a spiral and roll out again gently.
Cook on a hot dry pan for 2–3 minutes per side, brushing with oil, until golden spots appear. Serve warm.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ndengu or beef stew.

description: A rich, sticky sweet from Kenya's coast made with ghee, flour, sugar and cardamom—served at celebrations and festivals.

steps.instruction: Melt the ghee in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add the flour and roast, stirring constantly, until golden brown and fragrant, about 8–10 minutes.
In a separate pot, combine sugar, water and cardamom. Bring to a boil to make a syrup.
Carefully pour the hot syrup into the roasted flour mixture, stirring vigorously to prevent lumps.
Cook on low heat, stirring, for 8–10 minutes until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pan. Serve warm or at room temperature.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a dessert after a coastal meal.

description: Soft Kenyan fried dough enriched with butter, milk and a little sugar—a teatime favourite across the country.

steps.instruction: Rub the butter into the flour and salt until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Stir in the sugar.
Add the milk and egg (if using) and mix into a soft dough. Knead gently for 3–4 minutes.
Cover and let rest for 15 minutes. Roll out and cut into triangles or squares.
Fry in hot oil for 2–3 minutes per side until golden brown. Drain and serve warm.

serving_suggestion: Serve with tea or coffee.

description: A traditional Kalenjin fermented milk, slightly sour and smooth, served as a nutritious drink or accompaniment to ugali.

steps.instruction: Bring the fresh milk to a boil, then remove from heat and let it cool to lukewarm.
Stir in the sour milk as a starter culture.
Pour into a clean calabash or jar, cover and leave in a warm place for 1–2 days to ferment until thick and sour.
Stir well and serve chilled or at room temperature.

serving_suggestion: Serve alongside ugali or as a refreshing drink.

description: A hearty Kenyan stew of green plantains simmered with beef, tomatoes and onions until tender and flavourful.

steps.instruction: Peel the green plantains and cut into chunks. Soak in water to prevent browning.
Heat oil and brown the beef cubes for 6–8 minutes. Add chopped onions and garlic and cook until soft.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce.
Add the plantains, salt and water. Cover and simmer for 25–30 minutes until the plantains are tender and the stew has thickened.
Serve hot with rice or as a standalone meal.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or chapati.

name_en: Kenyan Ripe Plantain and Beef Stew
description: Sweet ripe plantains cooked with tender beef in a rich tomato sauce—a comforting Kenyan stew with a balance of sweet and savoury.

steps.instruction: Peel the ripe plantains and cut into thick slices. Brown the beef in hot oil for 6–8 minutes.
Add chopped onion and garlic and cook until softened. Stir in chopped tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add the plantains, salt and water. Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes until the plantains are soft and the beef is tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with rice or ugali.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or chapati.

description: Bright, tangy Kenyan rice made with fresh lemon juice and zest, a simple side that pairs well with stews and grilled meats.

steps.instruction: Rinse the rice. Heat oil and sauté chopped onion (if using) until soft.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute. Pour in water and add salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 18–20 minutes until the rice is tender.
Squeeze the lemon juice over the cooked rice and grate in some zest. Fluff gently and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with grilled fish or chicken stew.

description: A tangy, spicy lime pickle from Mombasa, made with lime slices, turmeric, chilli and oil—a condiment for rice and curries.

steps.instruction: Wash and thinly slice the limes. Mix with salt and turmeric in a bowl.
Pack the lime mixture tightly into a clean glass jar.
Heat oil in a small pan and add the chilli flakes. Pour the hot oil over the limes.
Seal the jar and leave in a warm place for 2–3 days to mature before using.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a condiment with pilau, biryani or grilled fish.

description: A whole chicken spatchcocked and grilled over charcoal, marinated with lemon, garlic and paprika—a Kenyan celebration favourite.

steps.instruction: Spatchcock the chicken by cutting along the backbone and flattening it. Pat dry.
Mix lemon juice, crushed garlic, paprika, oil and salt into a marinade. Rub all over the chicken and let sit for 20 minutes.
Grill over medium charcoal or on a barbecue for 30–40 minutes, turning occasionally, until the skin is charred and the chicken is cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into pieces and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with kachumbari and ugali.

description: A coastal Kenyan chicken curry with chicken breast simmered in a spiced coconut sauce, finished with fresh coriander.

steps.instruction: Cut the chicken breast into chunks and season with salt. Heat oil and brown the chicken for 4–5 minutes, then remove.
Sauté onion, garlic and ginger until fragrant. Stir in curry powder and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a simmer. Return the chicken to the pan and cook for 15 minutes until tender and the sauce thickens.
Stir in chopped coriander and serve hot with rice or chapati.

serving_suggestion: Serve with coconut rice or chapati.

description: A fragrant Kenyan coastal biryani made with chicken thighs, basmati rice and warming spices, layered and steamed.

steps.instruction: Marinate the chicken thighs with yogurt, garlic, ginger, pilau masala and salt for 30 minutes.
Par-boil the rice in salted water until half-cooked, then drain.
Fry the onions until golden. Add the marinated chicken and cook until browned and cooked through.
Layer the chicken and rice in a heavy pot, cover tightly and steam on low heat for 20 minutes.
Fluff gently and serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with kachumbari or raita.

description: A rustic Kenyan stew of free-range chicken drumsticks simmered with onions, tomatoes and simple spices until tender.

steps.instruction: Heat oil in a pot and brown the chicken drumsticks on all sides for 6–8 minutes.
Add chopped onions and garlic and cook until soft and golden.
Add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook until the tomatoes break down into a sauce.
Add water, cover and simmer on low heat for 30–35 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Serve hot with ugali or rice.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and greens.

description: Beef liver sliced and pan-fried with onions, tomatoes and a touch of garlic—a quick, nutritious Kenyan dish.

steps.instruction: Slice the liver into thin strips and rinse. Pat dry.
Heat oil and sauté the onion until softened. Add garlic if using and cook for 1 minute.
Add the liver and cook on high heat for 3–4 minutes until browned.
Add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook for 5–7 minutes until the tomatoes break down and the liver is cooked through. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and spinach.

description: Tender beef tripe slow-cooked in a rich tomato-onion gravy—a beloved Kenyan comfort dish often served with ugali.

steps.instruction: Clean the tripe thoroughly and boil in salted water for 1 to 1.5 hours until very tender. Cut into strips.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and curry powder (if using) and cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened into a sauce.
Add the boiled tripe and stir to coat. Simmer for 10–15 minutes, adding a little water if needed. Adjust salt and serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and sukuma wiki.

description: Beef ribs boiled until tender then fried in a thick tomato and onion sauce—a hearty Kenyan wet fry.

steps.instruction: Boil the beef ribs in salted water for 45–50 minutes until tender. Reserve the broth.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a thick sauce.
Add the boiled ribs and a splash of reserved broth. Stir-fry for 10–15 minutes until the ribs are coated and the sauce is thick. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and greens.

description: Smoked fish simmered in a rich tomato and onion sauce, a specialty of Kenya's lakeside communities.

steps.instruction: Soak the smoked fish in warm water for 10 minutes to remove excess salt. Drain and cut into pieces.
Heat oil and sauté onions until soft. Add garlic if using and cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they form a sauce.
Add the fish and water. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until the fish is heated through and the sauce is flavorful. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali or matoke.

description: A traditional Luhya and Luo stew of dried fish cooked with tomatoes and onions, served with ugali.

steps.instruction: Soak the dried fish in warm water for 10 minutes, then clean and remove any bones.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened.
Add the fish and water. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until the fish is tender and the stew has thickened.
Season with salt and serve hot with ugali.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and greens.

description: A comforting Kenyan stew of black-eyed peas simmered with tomatoes, onions and gentle spices—often served over rice.

steps.instruction: Rinse the black-eyed peas and boil in water for 30–40 minutes until tender. Drain, reserving some liquid.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic if using and cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce.
Add the cooked peas and a little reserved liquid. Simmer for 10 minutes, season with salt and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve over rice or with chapati.

description: Yellow lentils simmered in creamy coconut milk with tomatoes and mild spices—a coastal Kenyan favourite.

steps.instruction: Rinse the yellow lentils. Heat oil and sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Add chopped tomatoes and curry powder (if using) and cook for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add the lentils, coconut milk, water and salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20–25 minutes until the lentils are soft and the stew is creamy.
Serve hot with rice or chapati.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or chapati.
